chunk_map.heading: # Painting the picture with the LLM
## Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read: chunk 1 (lines 3-11) — 'it' in 'The LLM is the infinite version of it' (L9) resolves to 'that argument about tools' one clause earlier in the same sentence; 'It was trained to match you' (L11) resolves to 'The LLM', named repeatedly above in the same chunk. Chunk 2 (lines 13-20) — 'You prime it. The LLM scales it.' (L16): 'it' resolves to 'the session', named the sentence before ('The session bends to what sits in the context window', L16); 'session' itself was introduced in chunk 1 ('what fits the session', L7) and reused across slides — explicitly NOT a violation per the rule's own carve-out. Shotgun/cannon (L20) is a self-contained, maintainer-attested unexplained image (maintainer L32: 'a deliberate provocation beat... the unexplained image is the point... do not cut, literalize, or replace with a named lever'), not a referent needing an antecedent — it introduces two fresh metaphors, it does not point at something undefined. Chunk 3 (lines 22-28) — 'your setup' (L24) is defined in the same sentence pair by apposition ('The rules and context you put in front of the LLM: can that stack learn...'), in-chunk. 'It'/'the setup' in the next paragraph (L26) resolve to 'your setup'/'that stack' one sentence earlier, same chunk. No never-named, vague, or stranded referents anywhere in the body.

All three body chunks carry multiple self-carrying sentences: chunk 1 (wizard/autocomplete transition, good/bad range, tool-vs-taste argument, stance-is-ceiling close), chunk 2 (prime-and-scale claim, the three-example enumeration, the shotgun/cannon koan), chunk 3 (two named, unpacked frontier questions plus the 'Let's go' kicker). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 1 header 'The LLM mirrors your stance' is restated verbatim at L7. Chunk 2 header 'You prime, the LLM scales' is restated verbatim at L16 ('You prime it. The LLM scales it.'). Chunk 3 header 'Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things' is cashed out by the chunk's own two named questions (L24, L26). No header is contradicted by its chunk's content.

Not-X-Not-Y-Z: none found; closest is 'Auto-complete was a thing. Auto-complete is no longer a thing.' (L5), a two-sentence before/after contrast, not the banned triadic-negation shape. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: shotgun/cannon (L20, 'If you want a shotgun, you have a shotgun. If you want a cannon, you have that too.') is a 2-leg pair, not a triple, and maintainer-attested as deliberate (L32); the following sentence ('The sharp engineers stay sharp.') is a distinct closing claim, not a repeated third leg. Self-grading superlatives: grepped and read manually — none present anywhere in the body; blocking sub-item clear. Number + retraction: no digits appear in the body at all (`sed -n '1,28p' curriculum/lectures/painting-the-picture-with-the-llm.md | grep -c '[0-9]'` -> 0), N/A. Abstraction-noun stacks: 'context window', 'stack', 'setup' are plain concrete engineering nouns with clear referents, not stacked abstractions. Verb triplets with an empty leg: L7 ('The LLM can do good work and bad work. It will be what fits the session. The LLM mirrors your stance.') has three sentences but three distinct, non-redundant predicates. Closest-to-violating specimen: L18, 'The rules file. The prompt. What sits on disk for the agent to read.' — a three-fragment enumeration, but each fragment names a genuinely distinct object (a file, a prompt, arbitrary on-disk content), so it is an example list rather than a repeated-frame anaphora template and survives the 'what does this concretely mean, alone' test per fragment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a lecture, so headings should be claims. Chunk 1 ('The LLM mirrors your stance') and chunk 2 ('You prime, the LLM scales') are full declarative claim sentences, each restated verbatim inside their own chunk content (L7, L16). Chunk 3's header, 'Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things,' is label/catalogue-shaped rather than a truth-claim sentence, but the compendium explicitly carves out 'catalogue entries naming their subject (Ralph, The numbers, Verification, named)' as NOT a violation — this header fits that shape (names its subject 'Two frontiers' with an appositive unpacking what they are, asserting no truth-claim the chunk's deliberately-unresolved content would then contradict). The chunk poses two open questions the maintainer's own delivery watch-for says must NOT be answered here (L100: 'Frontiers section names two open questions — do NOT answer them. The training answers by accretion through M1-M6.') — a preview/orientation header, not a consolidation slide where the header IS the teaching, so the claim requirement does not bind it.
No pointers to other files by position anywhere in the body. Godin is named-only, no location claim, no 'the opening lecture said' style callback.
